source: TSTD/MAFF Pumpkin (ល្ពៅ) Cultivation Manual, PDF title "10_Pumpkin_manual_body+covers" (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), 2012
text: Four fungal disease groups are covered for pumpkin. (1) Damping-off / seedling collapse, caused by soil/seed-borne fungi including Rhizoctonia solani, Pythium spp., and Fusarium spp. -- these pathogens can persist on seed and in soil, causing young seedlings to rot at the base and collapse within about 4-7 days of emergence in severe cases; prevention centers on treating seed with a protective fungicide dust before sowing and avoiding waterlogged nursery media. (2) Downy mildew, caused by Pseudoperonospora cubensis -- causes yellow, angular spots on leaves that expand and can cause leaf drying/death; favored by humid, wet conditions. (3) Powdery mildew, caused by Erysiphe cichoracearum and Sphaerotheca fuliginea -- appears as white/grey powdery spots on leaves that can spread to cover the whole leaf surface, reducing photosynthesis and vigor. (4) Fruit rot, associated with Choanephora cucurbitarum along with Pythium spp. and Rhizoctonia -- affects flowers and developing fruit, causing rot that can spread if infected material isn't removed. General prevention across all four: field sanitation (remove and destroy infected plant material), avoid overhead irrigation late in the day (reduces the humid window fungi need), avoid waterlogged soil, and use resistant/quality seed where available. For chemical control, the source names Mancozeb, Zineb, and Orthocide as seed-treatment/protective fungicides (used at roughly 3g per kg of seed for seed treatment) and metalaxyl+mancozeb, propineb, and copper hydroxide as options for treating active foliar disease outbreaks -- exact spray rates and intervals should be verified against the current product label before advising a farmer, since some of this detail was not confidently legible in the source scan.
caveat: Pathogen Latin names (Rhizoctonia solani, Pythium spp., Fusarium spp., Pseudoperonospora cubensis, Erysiphe cichoracearum, Sphaerotheca fuliginea, Choanephora cucurbitarum) and chemical names (Mancozeb, Zineb, Orthocide, metalaxyl, propineb, copper hydroxide) were clearly legible in the source and are transcribed with high confidence. However, the surrounding Khmer descriptive text (exact symptom wording, exact spray dosage/interval numbers) was heavily corrupted by the same CID/Limon font extraction issue affecting this whole document, so those details are described functionally rather than quoted -- verify precise application rates against the current registered product label before giving dosage advice to a farmer.
